title: Nasi Goreng
subtitle: Indonesian fried rice with kecap manis and fried egg
excerpt: Indonesia's national dish: wok-fried rice with sweet soy sauce, shallots, garlic, sambal, and a fried egg on top. The darkly caramelised kecap manis is the flavour that makes it instantly recognisable and nothing else quite replicates.

recipe.sourceNotes: Nasi goreng (literally 'fried rice' in Malay and Indonesian) is considered the national dish of Indonesia and is eaten at any time of day, typically as a way of using up leftover cooked rice. The defining flavour comes from kecap manis (a thick, sweet Indonesian soy sauce made with palm sugar), which caramelises in the hot wok and gives the rice its characteristic dark colour and sweet-salty depth. Sambal (chilli paste) provides the heat, and terasi (fermented shrimp paste, similar to belacan) adds umami funk; both can be adjusted to taste. The dish always comes topped with a fried egg with a runny yolk, often with fried shallots, cucumber, and tomato on the side. Day-old rice is essential — freshly cooked rice is too wet to fry properly.

content.text: Use cold, day-old rice; freshly cooked rice makes the dish wet and clumped. The wok must be very hot before adding the rice; add it in one layer, press it down, and leave it for 30 seconds to crisp slightly on the base before tossing. Kecap manis (sweet soy sauce) is not the same as dark soy sauce; if unavailable, mix equal parts dark soy sauce and honey.

items.preparation: cooked the day before and refrigerated
2 for the rice; 1 for frying as a topper per portion
kecap manis (sweet soy) preferred; or mix dark soy with 1 tsp honey

content.text: Heat 3 tablespoons of oil in a wok over the highest heat until smoking. Stir-fry the shallots, garlic, and chilli for 1 minute. Push to the side. Scramble the 2 beaten eggs in the centre, breaking them up as they set.

Add the cold rice. Press it into the wok and leave for 30 seconds. Toss. Add the dark and light soy sauces and sesame oil. Toss continuously for 2 minutes until the rice is heated through, dark, and slightly crispy in places.

Fry the remaining eggs separately in the remaining oil until the whites are set and the yolks are still runny. Divide the rice between bowls. Top each with a fried egg. Serve with sliced spring onion, cucumber, and extra chilli.
